# `drive.import`

Materialize your own Google Docs from registered folders and their subfolders, including resolved Doc shortcut targets (never folder shortcuts). (fetched agent-side via your host Drive tools; never called from here — no OVT Google credentials) into the local drive_export directory. Ownership is verified server-side per file: it must be a My-Drive item (drive_id null) owned solely by you (owners == [your owner_id]) — a Shared-Drive, multi-owner, or mismatched file is dropped, never accepted. Each revision is stored as its own immutable file (identity is file_id alone; revision is provenance). Accepts the {owner_id, sync_cursor, files} envelope inline or via --file; the CLI also falls back to stdin if neither is given.

- **group:** `mutation`
- **posture:** `reversible`
- **CLI:** `operator-voice drive-import`
- **MCP tool:** `drive_import` (mutation — hidden unless explicitly enabled)

## Arguments

| name | type | required | help |
|---|---|---|---|
| `owner_id` | `str` | optional, default=None | Your own Drive user id (self-asserted; verified per-file server-side) |
| `files` | `json` | optional, default=None | JSON list of {file_id, revision_id, drive_id, owners, mime_type, modified_time, owner_id, text, folder_id, via_shortcut?} — folder_id is the registered ancestor; shortcut entries carry the target's own metadata and text — alternative to --file |
| `sync_cursor` | `json` | optional, default=None | Opaque Drive Changes sync token {changes_page_token, new_start_page_token} to persist for the next incremental refresh (read back from drive.status) |
| `file` | `str` | optional, default=None | Path to a JSON file containing {owner_id, sync_cursor, files} (CLI convenience) |

## Examples

```
operator-voice drive-import --file /tmp/drive-envelope.json
```

## Errors

| code | what it means |
|---|---|
| `invalid_arguments` | An argument was missing, had the wrong type, or wasn't one of the allowed choices — nothing changed. |
| `owner_id_missing` | Your own Drive user id (the top-level owner_id) is required — supply it directly, or via --file/stdin as part of the {owner_id, files} envelope. |
| `no_files_provided` | No files were supplied — provide --files, --file, or pipe the envelope via stdin. |
| `import_file_not_found` | No file exists at the given --file path. |
| `import_file_not_valid_json` | The --file content (or piped stdin) was not valid JSON. |
